entities.summary: Themistocles was an Athenian politician and general. He was one of a new breed of non-aristocratic politicians who rose to prominence in the early years of the Athenian democracy. As a politician, Themistocles was a populist, having the support of lower-class Athenians, and generally being at odds with the Athenian nobility. Elected archon in 493 BC, he convinced the polis to increase the naval power of Athens, a recurring theme in his political career. During the first Persian invasion of Greece, he fought at the Battle of Marathon (490 BC), and may have been one of the ten Athenian strategoi (generals) in that battle.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: Themistocles played a crucial role in shaping Athenian democracy by convincing the polis to increase its naval power, which ultimately contributed to the defeat of the Persian invasion at Marathon (490 BC). This victory marked a significant turning point in Greek history and had far-reaching consequences for the development of Western civilization.
